headline: Hot inflation and new tariff proposals knocked the S&P 500 down 3.2% early Wednesday, but buyers took back almost all of it by the close. Chips still fell, and a December hike is now close to certain.
summary: No brief was published for Wednesday Nov 25; this one covers Tuesday and Wednesday. Closes here are Wednesday Nov 25 (the dashboard's prices_as_of is 2026-11-25, checked with Massive). Core PCE rose 3.3% from a year ago, a tenth over forecast, Q3 GDP was revised up to 4.3%, and futures now price about a 98% chance of a hike on Dec 9 (BEA; CNBC; Yahoo Finance via NorthTape). The same morning the US Trade Representative proposed tariffs of 15% to 35% on 14 economies, with India at up to 25% and its drug makers named, and Mexico left out (USTR). The S&P 500 fell as much as 3.2% to 6,970 and closed down only 0.25% at 7,182.78; the Dow closed higher and midcaps rose 1.2%, but Nvidia fell another 3.9% to 149.30 after S&P put its credit rating on watch (Benzinga; CNBC; Massive). Markets are closed today and close at 1pm ET Friday, so no move this week can confirm on volume.

regime.why: Two down days for the Nasdaq after Monday's surge, and the AI leaders keep making lower lows. Wednesday's recovery was broad (most S&P 500 stocks rose, midcaps +1.2%), which is a better sign than Monday's one stock rally. A follow through day needs a strong gain on higher volume on a full session; Friday's half day cannot count, so the earliest is Monday Nov 30.

signals.title: Hot core PCE and a 4.3% GDP make a December 9 hike close to certain
signals.what_happened: October PCE prices rose 0.3% for the month and 3.8% from a year ago; core rose 0.3% and 3.3%, up from 3.1% and a tenth over the forecast (BEA; CNBC via NorthTape). Personal income jumped 0.7% against 0.4% expected, Q3 GDP was revised to 4.3% from 3.4%, and jobless claims fell to 189,000 (MT Newswires via NorthTape). Traders priced about a 98% chance of a quarter point hike on Dec 9 and lean toward another in January (Yahoo Finance; Reuters via NorthTape). The Beige Book said growth was slight and contacts expect costs and prices to keep rising (Investing.com). Yet the 10 year yield fell 6 basis points to 4.86% as money bought bonds for safety (TheStreet).
signals.so_what: A strong economy with sticky inflation is a Fed that keeps hiking. Who pays: rate sensitive borrowers and the most expensive growth stocks. Who gets paid: savers and short term cash. The odd part is that long yields fell on the news. That says investors fear the hikes will slow growth later, or they wanted safety from the AI sell off. If long yields keep falling while the Fed hikes, the curve flattens, which has often come before a slowdown. What would make this wrong: a soft November jobs report on Dec 4 could pull January hike odds back.
signals.for_you: Swing: the utility setups (AEP, NI) and the defensive names on the MT scan do best when long yields fall, so Wednesday helped them; still wait for a close over the pivot on volume. Puts: VIX 28.29 keeps premiums rich, but no liquid put passed the screen. Long term: no change to the buy list from the data alone.

signals.title: New US tariffs proposed on 14 economies: India up to 25% with drug makers named, Mexico left out
signals.what_happened: The USTR found that 14 economies use unfair industrial policies under Section 301 and proposed tariffs on all their goods, net of existing duties, with exemptions: up to 35% on Vietnam, 25% on India (17% with a deal), 20% on China and Singapore, 18% on Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand, and 15% on the EU, Japan, Korea, Switzerland and Taiwan (USTR; Politico). Its India report names pharmaceuticals and medical devices first; the EU report names autos, chemicals and pharmaceuticals; Switzerland's names pharmaceuticals. Mexico and Norway were investigated but left out for now. Comments are due Jan 5, 2027 and hearings start Jan 25 (USTR).
signals.so_what: This is the next tariff wall, not a fight with one country. Who pays: US buyers of generic drugs, autos and electronics made abroad, and the exporters that sell them. Who gets paid: Mexico, whose factories gain if production moves away from the 14 named economies, and US makers that compete with imports. Second order: India is a major supplier of US generic drugs, so a 25% tariff would raise costs for pharmacies and insurers or squeeze the makers. Third order: these are proposals with deal discounts built in (India 17%, Vietnam 20%, Singapore 10%), so the real aim is leverage before late January, when the China metals pause also ends. US listed shares mostly rose by the close: RDY +1.2%, TM +2.8%, EWW +2.0% (Massive).
signals.for_you: Swing: RDY is the most exposed name on the dashboard. Its Wednesday close over the pivot came on 4,289,544 shares, a hair under the 4,298,000 needed, so it is not a confirmed entry, and the tariff risk is new. Wait. INDA closed exactly at its 53.20 level: volume passed but the close did not, so wait for a close over it. Puts: no puts on TM, HMC or other autos before the hearings. Long term: no change.

signals.title: Wednesday's round trip: a 3.2% drop erased by the close, but the AI leaders kept falling
signals.since_yesterday: S&P put Nvidia's AA credit rating on watch for a cut, and NVDA has now given back 9.5% of Monday's 31% jump.
signals.what_happened: The S&P 500 fell as much as 3.2% to 6,970.11 in the first half hour and closed down 0.25% at 7,182.78; the Dow rose, erasing a 1,100 point loss, and the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.62% (CNBC; Benzinga). Midcaps (MDY) rose 1.16% and equal weight Nasdaq 100 rose 0.24% while the Magnificent Seven ETF lost 1.05% (Market Scholars). NVDA fell as much as 9.1% and closed 149.30, down 3.9%; MU fell 4.5% to 601.25, 15% below Monday's close (Massive). S&P Global put Nvidia's AA rating on CreditWatch negative, saying the CEO's exit and return does not answer its questions on board oversight, and it could cut one notch within 90 days (S&P Global; CNBC).
signals.so_what: The money did not leave stocks on Wednesday; it left the AI leaders and went into everything else. That rotation is healthier than Monday's one stock rally. A credit watch on a company with huge cash matters little for its borrowing. It matters as a signal: a rating agency now treats governance as a real risk, which keeps big funds cautious. What would make this wrong: Nvidia's next report or a clean board review.
signals.for_you: Swing: no chip entries. NVDA is under its falling 200 day (202.62) with no buy point. Puts: no puts on NVDA, MU or SMH; they swing 5% to 15% a day. Long term: ENTG left the buy list after falling 9.6% in two days, a good reminder of why we waited for the PCE data.

signals.title: Earnings: Dell's record backlog, Deere's weak guide and a 15% drop in Nutanix
signals.what_happened: Dell's revenue rose 103% to $54.9 billion, AI server revenue was $22.0 billion, its AI backlog hit a record $132.3 billion, and it raised its full year revenue outlook to $202 billion (Dell; Reuters via NorthTape). DELL still closed 297.06 Wednesday, after an 11.8% drop Tuesday (Massive). HP Inc beat and raised its dividend, and closed up 11.5% at 31.15. Deere's 2027 profit forecast of $4.50 to $5.25 billion missed the $5.91 billion consensus (Reuters), yet DE closed up 4.4% at 641.02 (Massive). Ambarella guided its next quarter about 35% under estimates on memory costs (Benzinga). Nutanix fell 15.2% to 46.30 and Autodesk 3.5% (Massive).
signals.so_what: AI demand is still strong. The doubt is about what the buyers earn on it and how thin the server makers' margins get. Memory makers hold the scarce part, which is why HP and Ambarella both blamed memory costs. Deere is the opposite lesson: a bad guide with the bad news already in the price. DE had a confirmed break down on Nov 20 at 621.13 and has now closed back over that level.
signals.for_you: No action. No setups report next week. DE's Nov 20 break down has failed (it closed back over 621.13), so it is no longer a reason to block puts, but it has no buy point yet.

signals.title: Data check: an insider record from 2006, a breakout called at the level, and a setup listed under its stop
signals.what_happened: New problems in the Nov 25 data: (1) insiders.json lists SHMD with a trade dated 2006-11-25, a 'price' of 1,731,430 and a value of 2,147,483,647, which is the largest 32 bit number, so it is a parse error, and it sorts first by value. (2) buypoints.json calls INDA 'Closed over the level' when it closed exactly at 53.20, its level. (3) buypoints.json calls RDY's break 1.5x volume, while Massive shows 4,289,544 shares against setups.json's 4,298,000 needed; rounding turned 1.497x into 1.5x. (4) setups.json listed HLT on Nov 24 at 364.32, under its own 365.30 stop. (5) PYPL's zone top equals its close (57.81), and it is back on the buy list after its Nov 20 break down, now marked failed.
signals.so_what: Each of these makes a check pass when it should fail. A close at the level, or a volume ratio rounded up to 1.5x, is not her rule. A setup under its stop should be void, not new.
signals.for_you: Treat INDA and RDY as waits, HLT as close to void (it closed 366.20, 0.1% over its stop), and ignore SHMD. Each needs a fix with a test: compare close strictly over the level, compare raw volume to the share count, and drop setups whose price is under the stop.

cycle.quadrant: Inflation rising, growth holding up (Q3 growth was revised higher)
cycle.quadrant_why: Core PCE rose to 3.3% from 3.1%, headline PCE is 3.8%, Q3 GDP was revised to 4.3% and claims fell to 189,000 (BEA; MT Newswires via NorthTape). That is growth and inflation both running hot. It matches the All Weather model's season, so the model is not changed.
cycle.short_term_debt_cycle: Tightening and late. A Dec 9 hike is about 98% priced, futures lean toward January too, and the policy range is 3.75% to 4.00% (Yahoo Finance; Reuters via NorthTape).
cycle.long_term_debt_cycle: Late. Long yields fell on a hot inflation report, which says buyers want safety and expect the hikes to slow growth later.
cycle.big_cycle: External order: a new tariff wall on 14 economies, with deal discounts as leverage before late January. Technology: AI demand is strong but its returns are now doubted, and memory has become the scarce part. Internal order: a rating agency is questioning governance at the world's biggest chip company.
tailwinds: Broad buying Wednesday: most S&P 500 stocks rose and midcaps gained 1.2% (Market Scholars).
Mexico was left out of the tariff proposals.
headwinds: A December hike is close to certain, and January is in play.
Tariffs of 15% to 35% proposed on 14 economies.
AI leaders keep making lower lows.

history.what: The Fed doubled its rate from 3% to 6% into a strong economy. The 10 year yield rose from about 5.7% to about 8%, bonds had one of their worst years, and the S&P 500 fell about 9% from its high before ending the year near flat.
history.lesson: Hikes into strong growth hurt bonds and high priced stocks first, but they do not have to end in recession. The market bottomed while the Fed was still hiking.

cycle.differences: In 1994 inflation was near 3% and falling; today headline PCE is 3.8% and rising. In 1994 long yields jumped; this week they fell. And today's market leaders are a small group of AI stocks, which makes the index more fragile than in 1994.
cycle.for_you: Swing: favor the defensive setups the scans agree on, and only on a full session close with volume. Puts: premiums are rich, but wait for a liquid contract on a Buy zone now name. Long term: small pieces only, in names inside their zones and away from the tariff target list.
